title: Service Scope and Lifetime knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Service Scope and Lifetime”?
options: Service Scope and Lifetime means the browser can enforce all permissions without the backend.
Service Scope and Lifetime removes the need for error handling, accessibility checks and tests.
Service Scope and Lifetime should be implemented by copying a snippet without checking the Angular version.
Service Scope and Lifetime helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.answer_key: Service Scope and Lifetime helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.explanation: Service Scope and Lifetime is a concept in the supplied Angular curriculum. Its correct application depends on the intended behavior, surrounding context and verification.

questions.prompt: How should a learner work with “Application-wide services” in this lesson?
options: Assume “Application-wide services” works identically across every Angular major and runtime.
Use “Application-wide services” to bypass runtime validation of external or user-provided values.
Connect “Application-wide services” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
Treat “Application-wide services” as a reason to skip the surrounding application context.
questions.answer_key: Connect “Application-wide services” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.explanation: The PDF explicitly lists “Application-wide services” under Service Scope and Lifetime. Anchor it in a small example and check the behavior rather than relying on a memorized phrase.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest verification approach for “Service Scope and Lifetime”?
options: Ignore a failing test if the component looks correct in one browser.
Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
Assume an SVG diagram proves the code compiled and passed tests.
Treat a successful client-side render as backend authorization evidence.
questions.answer_key: Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.explanation: Verification evidence should match the running environment. Static teaching snippets are not compiler output, and frontend checks do not replace backend authorization.
